does: Lays a sheet of pastry over a filled dish, seals it to the rim and cuts a vent, so that the pastry bakes into a crisp lid while the filling steams underneath.
how: Let the filling cool a little, so that it does not melt the pastry before it reaches the oven.
Lay the pastry over the dish and press it onto the rim.
Trim the overhang and press the edge with a fork to seal it.
Cut a small slit in the middle for steam, and brush the top with beaten egg if you like.

cues.text: A lid sealed all round the rim, with a clear vent in the middle.
Cool, firm pastry that does not stick to the fingers.

mistakes.mistake: Laying pastry over a piping hot filling, so that it sags and turns soggy.
mistakes.fix: Let the filling cool for a while first.

mistakes.mistake: Forgetting the vent, so that steam bursts the lid or makes it soggy.
mistakes.fix: Always cut a slit in the middle.

comes_after.why: Home-made pastry is rolled out before it covers a dish.
